title: WNBA First-Round Playoffs Set Viewership Record: 1.3M Average Viewers, Up 37 Percent Year-Over-Year
dek: The WNBA's first-round playoffs averaged 1.3 million viewers across 10 games on ESPN, Prime Video, and USA Network, marking the most-watched opening round in league history. The viewership represents a 37 percent increase year-over-year and a 17 percent increase from the 2024 first-round record of 1.1 million average viewers.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: First-round average viewership of 1.3 million viewers across 10 games is the highest in WNBA history, up 37 percent from the prior year's 944,000 average over 11 games.
bottom_line: The league has secured its highest first-round viewership in history under the new media deal and across four partners rather than one. The test ahead is whether these numbers hold in the second round and conference finals, or whether the first-round spike was concentrated in Fever games and will decline as the field narrows.
body:
The WNBA's first-round playoffs delivered the league's most-watched opening round in history, according to Front Office Sports' reporting. The 10 games across ESPN, Prime Video, and USA Network averaged 1.3 million viewers, a 37 percent increase from the prior year's 944,000 average across 11 games.
The 2026 first-round average also exceeded the previous record set in 2024, when eight games averaged 1.1 million viewers. This year's first round exceeded 2024's performance by 17 percent, according to Front Office Sports.
According to Yahoo WNBA's reporting, Caitlin Clark's three Fever games made up the first round's three biggest audiences. Clark played her first postseason during the 2024 playoffs as a member of the Fever, which marked her rookie year in the league.
The 2026 playoffs are the league's first under a new media rights deal worth more than $3 billion, according to Front Office Sports. The deal splits postseason broadcast rights among four partners: ESPN, Amazon, NBC, and Versant. ESPN previously held exclusive rights to the playoffs. During the regular season, ESPN saw a 17 percent increase and CBS reported a 9 percent increase compared to the prior year, per Front Office Sports.
The expanded distribution across multiple broadcast partners marks a structural shift in how the league reaches audiences. The first-round numbers suggest the multi-platform approach is resonating with viewers.
